subject.title: Gateway becomes slow or times out under multi-session / multi-agent load

question: Should this issue remain the broad Gateway liveness tracker, or should maintainers split and route the remaining work to narrower canonical issues such as raw active transcript caps, channel no-settlement deadlines, and handler-specific live repros?
rationale: The codebase has partial fixes on main, but the remaining failure shape crosses Gateway RPC handlers, session storage retention, compaction, and channel delivery; only maintainers can choose the tracking and product-policy boundary before repair automation is safe.

options.title: Keep Umbrella With Live Proof Plan
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical broad tracker and require a current-main large-state replay that records handler latencies, event-loop delay, queued-message counts, and session-store scale before deciding what to fix next.

options.title: Split To Narrow Canonicals
options.body: Route raw transcript caps, channel deadlines, and any measured slow handler into separate canonical issues, then leave this issue only as the cross-linking umbrella or close it after all slices are owned.

options.title: Close Only After Current-Main Proof
options.body: Close this issue only if maintainers can show current main or a shipped release handles the reported workload without Gateway RPC timeouts or message delivery stalls.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella With Live Proof Plan
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical broad tracker and require a current-main large-state replay that records handler latencies, event-loop delay, queued-message counts, and session-store scale before deciding what to fix next.
